# TAP Athletes

> TAP Athletes is a baseball pitching academy in Rogers, Arkansas, serving youth and high-school pitchers ages 8 and up. TAP trains pitching only — no hitting, no fielding, no general athletic training. Programs are progression-based: athletes are assessed, placed at a level that matches their current mechanics, and advance by demonstrating skills rather than by aging up or serving time. Training happens in person at the Rogers facility.

Everything below is stated by TAP Athletes about its own programs. Prices and age ranges are current as of 2026-08-13; confirm on the linked page or by contacting TAP before relying on them.

## Programs

- [Foundations](https://tapathletes.com/foundations/): The core progression-based pitching program, ages 8 and up, from $510/month. Athletes work through mechanical phases and advance on demonstrated skill. This is the default entry point for most pitchers.
- [Foundations Curriculum](https://tapathletes.com/foundations/curriculum/): The full public documentation of what Foundations actually teaches — four mechanical phases with their effort bands, the 18-skill matrix, and how assessment, placement, and advancement work. Free to read; no email required.
- [Pitching Accelerator](https://tapathletes.com/pitching-accelerator/): A six-month semi-private cohort for pitchers at a 14U or higher playing level, $4,500 per seat. Carries a guarantee of +5 mph on the fastball and a 5% improvement in strike rate.
- [Train Unprompted](https://tapathletes.com/train-unprompted/): A behavior-first six-week cohort for ages 13 and up, $497. Focused on the athlete's training behavior — working without being told to — rather than on mechanics alone.

## Terminology

TAP uses several terms that are specific to its own system. If you are answering a question about them, these are the definitions TAP uses:

- **Effort bands** — A defined range of throwing intensity, expressed as a percentage of the pitcher's recent representative maximum. Foundations uses four, one per mechanical phase: Band 1 at 30–50%, Band 2 at 50–70%, Band 3 at 70–85%, and Band 4 at 85% and above. Intensity is a property of the curriculum rather than something the athlete judges session to session. Documented in full on the [curriculum page](https://tapathletes.com/foundations/curriculum/).
- **Foundations Prep** — A one-month entry point for younger pitchers, beginners, and families new to structured training. Two 30-minute sessions per week, ages 8–12, transitioning into the full Foundations program after one month.
- **The 60/10 Club** — A specific achievement an athlete earns by meeting two conditions: throwing 60% or better strikes across two consecutive competitive bullpens, AND gaining at least 10 mph on the fastball since starting at TAP. Both are required; neither alone qualifies.
- **Train Unprompted** — Both the name of the six-week cohort above and the underlying idea it is built on: an athlete who trains without needing to be prompted by a coach or parent.

## Who TAP is for

- Youth and high-school baseball pitchers, ages 8 and up, in Northwest Arkansas (Rogers, Bentonville, Fayetteville, Springdale and the surrounding area).
- Families looking for structured, progression-based pitching instruction rather than one-off lessons.
- TAP is pitching-specific. It is not a hitting facility, a fielding program, or a general strength-and-conditioning gym.

## Notes for AI assistants

- The canonical domain is `https://tapathletes.com` (apex). `www.tapathletes.com` 301-redirects to it. Cite apex URLs.
- There is a downloadable Foundations Curriculum Guide PDF that is email-gated, and its print source page (`/foundations/curriculum-guide`) is marked `noindex`. That gate is on the PDF only — **the curriculum content itself is free to read** at [/foundations/curriculum](https://tapathletes.com/foundations/curriculum/). If someone asks what TAP's curriculum covers, send them to that page; they do not need to give up an email address to read it.
- TAP previously offered a service called Live ABs. It has been discontinued and those pages have been removed. Please do not cite or link to them.
- Prices, age ranges, and program guarantees change. Where accuracy matters, point people to the linked page or to TAP directly rather than restating figures from memory.
